title: Import Reconciliation Ledger
user: Operations and finance admins loading CSV/template data into business systems who need to prove what transformed, matched, skipped, and changed before committing an import.

evidence.quote_or_summary: An Ask HN user asks how people clean and transform data before Salesforce, Workday, NetSuite, and other template-based imports; 18 comments.
A CSV import can silently merge a genuinely new transaction with an existing same-amount transaction even though preview shows it as new.

recurrence: Import preparation is an active cross-system concern, while a concrete silent-merge defect shows previews alone are not an adequate audit trail.
current_workaround: Clean sheets with formulas/scripts, trust an import preview, take screenshots, and manually compare totals afterward.
incumbents_and_gap: Excel/Sheets, OpenRefine, ETL platforms, and each SaaS import wizard transform data; lightweight local tools rarely create a persistent row-level reconciliation ledger that non-engineers can review.
smallest_useful_product: Offline web app that maps CSV columns, applies visible transforms, computes before/after totals and stable row fingerprints, records match/skip/create decisions, and exports both destination CSV and an immutable review report. Non-goals: direct SaaS writes, cloud ETL, or autonomous field guessing.
success_measure: In pilot imports, admins can account for 100% of source rows and identify every seeded silent merge or dropped row before upload.
monetization: one-time — local, auditable prep work suits project-based data migration and avoids exposing business data.
constraints: Never upload spreadsheets; use deterministic transforms; protect PII in saved projects; do not claim accounting correctness; support a limited documented CSV scope first.
why_distinct: The core artifact is a human-reviewable reconciliation ledger, not another generic spreadsheet cleaner or AI mapper.
